data.heading: Rainforests
data.text: Rainforests are the wettest places on Earth.
Tropical rainforests are much wetter than temperate rainforests.
The emergent zone has giant trees that receive lots of sunlight and are home to birds and insects.
The canopy zone has smaller trees, which receive less sunlight. These house lots of mammals and reptiles as well as birds and insects.
The understorey is home to smaller plants. It gets little sunlight but lots of moisture.
The forest floor is the ground where large animals and lots of insects live. Very little sunlight reaches the floor.
